newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says no capital flight since fx rules relaxed.
newsitem.headline: Israel says no capital flight since fx rules relaxed.

text.p: Foreign currency liberalisation by Israel in the last decade has not caused a flight of capital from the country, the central bank said on Monday.

The central bank's monetary department said the liberalisation process had significantly increased opportunities for the public and the business sector to invest in foreign currency assets in Israel and overseas.

"This process did not cause the export of capital from Israel. On the contrary, the amount of foreign currency assets and assets linked to foreign currency held by the public has fallen from 18 percent at the beginning of the decade to 10 percent today," the central bank said.
The liberalisation process which started at the end of the 1980s -- with the government allowing mutual funds to invest in foreign equities -- continues to date.

"The erosion, in real terms, of the exchange rate and the transition from an expansionary monetary policy to a tight one, along with a rise, in real terms, of interest rates on the shekel to maintain the inflation target, all caused returns on foreign currency assets to be lower than returns on shekel-linked assets," the central bank said.
